questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pressure in a reservoir of water is same at all points at the same level of water.

Statement II: The pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted in all directions equally.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$& are false
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pressure in a static fluid will be same at each point on same horizontal level.

$P = {P}_{0} + ρgh$

where~${P}_{0}$& is atmospheric pressure.

Pascal's law states that pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted equally in all directions. Hence, both the statements are true and this is the right option.

questions.q: Water flows into a large tank with flat bottom at the rate of ${10}^{- 4}m^{3}s^{- 1} .$ Water is also leaking out of a hole of area $1cm^{2}$ at its bottom. If the height of the water in the tank remains steady then this height is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Amount of water going out = amount of water coming in.

$\sqrt{2gh} \times A = V$

$h = \dfrac{{\left({10}^{- 4}\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 9.8 \times {\left({10}^{- 4}\right)}^{2}} = 5.1cm$

questions.q: Two small drops of mercury each of radius $R$& coalesce to form a single large drop. The ratio of total surface energy before and after the change is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} + \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{' 3}$

$R^{'} = 2\dfrac{1}{3}R \ldots \left(i\right)$

${A}_{i} = 2 \left[4\piR^{2}\right]$

${A}_{f} = 4\piR^{' 2}$

$\dfrac{Ui}{Uf} = \dfrac{Ai}{Af} = \dfrac{2R^{2}}{{2}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}R^{2}} ===2\dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.q: The terminal velocity  \left({v}_{t}\right)$~of the spherical rain drop depends on the radius  \left(r\right)$ of the spherical rain drop as&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity of a sphere of radius& $r$~and density~$ρ$, immersed in a liquid of density~$\sigma$~and viscosity~$η$~is given by~${v}_{T} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{\left(ρ - \sigma\right)r^{2}g}{η}$

Hence, for spherical raindrop,~${v}_{T} ∝ r^{2}$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
Statement II : The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube does not depend on the inner radius of the tube.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct as we know contact angle depends on cohesine and adhesive forces.
Statement II is incorrect because height of liquid is given by $h==\frac{2 T \cos \theta_C}{\rho g r}$ where $r$ is radius of Tube (assuming length of capillary is sufficient).

questions.q: Consider a completely full cylindrical water tank of height 1.6 m and cross-sectional area $0.5 \mathrm{~m}^2$. It has a small hole in its side at a height 90 cm from the bottom. Assume, the cross-sectional area of the hole to be negligibly small as compared to that of the water tank. If a load 50 kg is applied at the top surface of the water in the tank then the velocity of the water coming out at the instant when the hole is opened is :  \left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Apply Bernouli equation between points $1 \ \text{ and } 2$
$\begin{aligned}
& P_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2+\rho g h=P_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2+0 \\ & P_0+\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{~A}}+\rho g \frac{70}{100}=P_0+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2 \\ & \frac{5000}{0.5}+10^3 \times 10 \frac{70}{100}=\frac{1}{2} \times 10^3 v_2^2
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& 10^3+10^3 \times 7=\frac{10^3}{2} \mathrm{v}_2^2 \\ & \mathrm{v}_2^2=16 \\ & \mathrm{v}_2=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
As the tank area is large $\mathrm{v}_1$ is negligible compared to $\mathrm{v}_2$

questions.q: Consider a solid sphere of radius $R$ and mass density $ρ\left(r\right) = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right), 0 < r \le R .$ The minimum density of a liquid in which it will float is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The density of any point inside the sphere is

$ρ = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right)0 < r \le R$

weight = buoyant force
mg = B

$mg = {ρ}_{L}Vg$
$∫ ρ\left(4\pir^{2}dr\right)g = {ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}g$
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}{ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right)4\pir^{2}dr = {ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}{ρ}_{0}4\pi\left(r^{2} - \dfrac{r^{4}}{R^{2}}\right)dr = {ρ}_{0}4\pi{\left(\dfrac{r^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{r^{5}}{5R^{2}}\right)}_{0}^{R} = {ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$
$\dfrac{2}{5}{ρ}_{0} = {ρ}_{L}$

questions.q: A small ball of mass $m$ and density $\rho$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density $\rho_0$. After sometime, the ball falls with constant velocity. The viscous force on the ball is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{ma}\mathrm{a}=0$ for constant velocity
$\begin{aligned}
& m g-F_B=F_v \\
& F_v=m g-v \rho_0 g=m g-\frac{m}{\rho} \rho_0 g=m g\left(1-\frac{\rho_0}{\rho}\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An air bubble of radius 0.1 cm lies at a depth of 20 cm below the free surface of a liquid of density $1000 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. If the pressure inside the bubble is $2100 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$ greater than the atmospheric pressure, then the surface tension of the liquid in SI unit is (use $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P_1=P_0+\rho g h=P_0+1000 \times 10 \times \frac{20}{100} \\ & \Rightarrow P_1=P_0+2000 \end{aligned}$ So, $P_2-P_1=\frac{2 S}{R}=\left(\frac{2 S}{1 \times 10^{-3}}\right)\Rightarrow P_2=P_0+2100$ (given) $\begin{aligned} & \text { So, } P_0+2100-P_0-2000=2 S \times 10^3 \\ & \Rightarrow 100=2 S \times 10^3 \\ & \Rightarrow s=\left(\frac{1}{20}\right)=0.05 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A liquid of density $\rho$ is coming out of a hose pipe of radius a with horizontal speed $v$ and hits a mesh. $50 \%$ of the liquid passes through the mesh unaffected. $25 \%$ looses all of its momentum and $25 \%$ comes back with the same speed. The resultant pressure on the mesh will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Mass per unit time of the liquid = \rhoav Momentum per second carried by liquid $=\rho a v \times v$ Net force due to bounced back liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{1}=2 \times $\left[\frac{1}{4} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}] Net force due to stopped liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{4} pav ^{2}$ Total force, $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{F}_{1}+\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}+\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}=\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2} Net pressure =\frac{3}{4} \rho$v^{2}

questions.q: An air bubble of volume $1{cm}^{3}$~rises from the bottom of a lake $40m$ deep to the surface at a temperature of $12 ° C .$ The atmospheric pressure is ~$1 \times {10}^{5}Pa,$ the density of water is $1000kgm^{- 3}$ and $g = 10ms^{- 2} .$There is no difference of the temperature of water at the depth of $40m$ and on the surface. The volume of air bubble when it reaches the surface will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The pressure at the bottom of the lake can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{P}_{bottom} & = & {P}_{0} + ρgh \\ & = & \left({10}^{5} + 1000 \times 10 \times 40\right)Pa \\ & = & 5 \times {10}^{5}Pa\end{cases}$

As the temperature of water remains constant, it can be written that

${P}_{bottom}{V}_{bottom} = {P}_{top}{V}_{top} . . . ( 1 )$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface.

$\begin{cases}5 \times {10}^{5} \times 1 & = & 1 \times {10}^{5} \times {V}_{top} \\ & ⇒ & {V}_{top} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{5} \times 1}{1 \times {10}^{5}}{cm}^{3} \\ & = & 5{cm}^{3}\end{cases}$

questions.q:
A water drop of radius $1\mum$ falls in a situation where the effect of buoyant force is negligible. Co-efficient of viscosity of air is $1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}Nsm^{- 2}$ and its density is negligible as compared to that of water ${10}^{6}gm^{- 3}$. Terminal velocity of the water drop is

(Take acceleration due to gravity $= 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity is given by& ${v}_{T} = \dfrac{2r^{2}\left(ρ - \sigma\right)g}{9η}$, where,~$r$~is radius of falling body,~$ρ$~is density of falling body and~$\sigma$~is density of fluid.

$⇒ {v}_{T} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 12} \times {10}^{6} \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10}{9 \times 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}}$

$⇒ {v}_{T} = 123 . 4 \times {10}^{- 6}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A air bubble of radius $1\text{cm}$ in water has an upward acceleration of $9.8{\text{cms}}^{– 2}$. The density of water is $1{\text{gm cm}}^{– 3}$ and water offers negligible drag force on the bubble. The mass of the bubble is  \left(g = 980\text{cm} / s^{2}\right)$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${F}_{b} - mg = ma$

${F}_{b} = m \left(g + a\right)$

=\dfrac{4}{3}{πr}^{3}$ρg = m \left(g + a\right)$

$m = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \left($1\right)g = m \left($980 + 9 .8\right)$

$m = 4 . 15

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: Statement I : When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation $P_1-P_2=\rho g \left(h_2-h_1\right)$. Statement II : In ventury tube shown $2 \mathrm{gh}=v_1^2-v_2^2
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.$
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation $\mathrm{P}_1+\rho \mathrm{gh}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\rho \mathrm{gh}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\left[h_1 \& h_2\right.$ are height of point from any reference level] Given $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2=0$ (for statement-1) $\therefore \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_2=\mathrm{g} \left(\mathrm{h}_2-\mathrm{h}_2\right)$
For statement-2 $\mathrm{P}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}}_{1}^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \m$mathrm{v}_2^2$\begin{aligned}& P_1-P_2=\rho g h \\ & P_1-P_2=\frac{1}{2} \rhov_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rhov_1^2 \\ & \rho g h=\frac{1}{2} \rhov_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rhov_1^2 \\ & 2 g h=v_2^2-v_1^2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A glass tumbler having inner depth of $17 . 5cm$ is kept on a table. A student starts pouring water  \left(\mu = \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$ into it while looking at the surface of water from the above. When he feels that the tumbler is half filled, he stops pouring water. Up to what height, the tumbler is actually filled ?$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Height of water observed by observer
$= \dfrac{H}{\muw} = \dfrac{H}{( 4 / 3 )} = \dfrac{3H}{4}$

Height of air observed by observer $= 17 . 5 - H$

According to question, both height observed by observer is same.
$\dfrac{3H}{4} = 17 . 5 - H$

$⇒ H = 10cm$

questions.q: In an experiment to verify Stokes law, a small spherical ball of radius& $r$ and density $ρ$ falls under gravity through a distance $h$ in air before entering a tank of water. If the terminal velocity of the ball inside water is same as its velocity just before entering the water surface, then the value of $h$ is proportional to: (ignore viscosity of air)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The velocity of ball just before striking& the surface of water& is given by using kinematical equation of motion under the gravity

$v^{2} = u^{2} - 2gy$

$⇒ v^{2} = - 2g ( - h )$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{2gh} . . . ( 1 )$~

Now, the terminal velocity of spherical ball inside the water tank is given by,

${v}_{T} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{r^{2} ( ρ - \sigma ) g}{η} . . . ( 2 )$

After falling through~$h$~the velocity of ball~should be equal to its terminal velocity.

From equation (1) and (2) we get,

$⇒ \sqrt{2gh} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{r^{2} ( ρ - \sigma ) g}{η}$

Squaring the above equation, we get

$⇒ h = \dfrac{2}{81}\dfrac{r^{4}g ( ρ - \sigma{)}^{2}}{η2}$

$⇒ h ∝ r^{4}$

questions.q:
The figure shows a liquid of given density flowing steadily in horizontal tube of varying cross-section. Cross-sectional areas at& $A$~is $1 . 5{cm}^{2},$~and $B$ is $25{mm}^{2},$ if the speed of liquid at $B$ is $60cms^{- 1}$ then $( {P}_{A} – {P}_{B} )$ is

(Given~${P}_{A}$~and~${P}_{B}$~are liquid pressures at $A$ and $B$ points.

Density~$ρ = 1000kgm^{- 3}$

$A$~and~$B$& are on the axis of tube)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Bernoulli's theorem,

${P}_{A} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_A^{2} = {P}_{B} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_B^{2} . . . ( i )$

Using equation of continuity,

${A}_{A}{V}_{A} = {A}_{B}{V}_{B}$

So,~$1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4} \times {V}_{A} = 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {V}_{B}$

${V}_{A} = \dfrac{25 \times {10}^{- 6}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} \times 0 . 6$

$= \dfrac{1}{10}ms^{- 1}$

Substituting in equation (i)

$⇒ {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \dfrac{1000}{2}\left[0 . {6}^{2} - 0 . {1}^{2}\right] = \dfrac{1000}{2} \times 0 . 7 \times 0 . 5$

$= 175Pa$

questions.q: A submarine experiences a pressure of $5.05 \times {10}^{6}Pa$ at a depth of ${d}_{1}$ in a sea. When it goes further to a depth of ${d}_{2}$ , it experiences a pressure of $8.08 \times {10}^{6}Pa$ . Then ${d}_{2} - {d}_{1}$ is approximately (density of water $= {10}^{3}kg / m^{3}$ and acceleration due to gravity $= 10ms^{- 2}$ ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The pressure at a depth $d$ is $p = {p}_{0} + ρgd$, here~${p}_{0}$~is the atmospheric pressure.
$∴ {p}_{1} = {p}_{0} + ρg{d}_{1}$
and~${p}_{2} = {p}_{0} + ρg{d}_{2}$
The difference in pressure is~${p}_{2} - {p}_{1} = ρg \left({d}_{2} - {d}_{1}\right)

Putting the values in the above equation
$8.08 $\times {10}^{6} -$5.05 $\times {10}^{6} = {10}^{3} \times$10 \left({d}_{2} - {d}_{1}\right)$
${d}_{2} - {d}_{1} = \dfrac{3.03 \times {10}^{6}}{104}$
$= 303m$&

$

questions.q:
A spherical ball of radius $1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}$ and density $10^5 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ falls freely under gravity through a distance $h$ before entering a tank of water, If after entering in water the velocity of the ball does not change, then the value of $h$ is approximately:
(The coefficient of viscosity of water is $9.8 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~s} / \mathrm{m}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~g}}{9} \frac{\mathrm{R}^2\left[\rho_{\mathrm{B}}-\rho_{\mathrm{L}}\right]}{\eta} \& \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{2}{9} \times \frac{10 \times\left(10^{-4}\right)^2}{9.8 \times 10^{-6}}\left[10^5-10^3\right] \& \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}=224.5\end{aligned}$
when ball fall from height (h)
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{V}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}} \\
& \mathrm{h}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\right)=2518 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A hydraulic press can lift $100$ kg when a mass $m$~is placed on the smaller piston. It can lift kg when the diameter of the larger piston is increased by $4$ times and that of the smaller piston is decreased by $4$ times keeping the same mass $m$& on the smaller piston.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Pascals law,&

$\dfrac{100 \times g}{A2} = \dfrac{mg}{A1} . . . \left(1\right)$

Let $m$ mass can lift ${M}_{0}$ in second case then

\dfrac{{M}_{0}g}{16{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{mg}{{A}_{1} / 16} . . . \left(2\right)$

\left\{SinceA = $\dfrac{\pid^{2}}{4}\right

From equation \left(1\right)$ and \left(2\right)$ we get

\dfrac{M0}{16 . 100} =$16$

$⇒ {M}_{0} = 25600kg$

$

questions.q:
A vessel with square cross-section and height of 6 m is vertically partitioned. A small window of $100 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ with hinged door is fitted at a depth of 3 m in the partition wall. One part of the vessel is filled completely with water and the other side is filled with the liquid having density $1.5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. What force one needs to apply on the hinged door so that it does not get opened ?
(Acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
in equilibrium
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{F}_{\text {ext }}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{w}}=\mathrm{F}_{\ell} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{F}_{\text {ext }}=\mathrm{F}_{\ell}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{w}} \\ & =\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\rho_{\ell} \mathrm{gh}\right) \mathrm{A}-\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\rho_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{gh}\right) \mathrm{A} \\ & =\left(\rho_{\ell}-\rho_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \mathrm{ghA} \\ & =(1500-1000) \times 10 \times 3 \times\left(100 \times 10^{-4}\right) \\ & =150 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Glycerin of density $1 . 25 \times {10}^{3}kgm^{– 3}$ is flowing through the conical section of pipe. The area of cross-section of the pipe at its ends are $10{cm}^{2}$ and~$5{cm}^{2}$~and pressure drop across its length is $3Nm^{– 2}$. The rate of flow of glycerine through the pipe is $x \times {10}^{– 5}m^{3}s^{– 1}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that

${A}_{1} = 10{cm}^{2}; {A}_{2} = 5{cm}^{2}$

$∆ P = 3Nm^{- 2}$

By continuity equation,

${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2} ⇒ {v}_{1} = \dfrac{{A}_{2}{v}_{2}}{A1} . . . ( i )$

By Bernoulli's equation,

$\dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v2}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v1}^{2} = ∆ P . . . ( ii )$

Using equation (i) in (ii)

$∆ P = \dfrac{ρ}{2} ( v^{2}2 - \left(\dfrac{{A}_{2}{v}_{2}}{A1}\right)2 ) ⇒ ∆ P = \dfrac{ρv^{2}2}{2}\left(1 - \left(\dfrac{A2}{A1}\right)2\right) ⇒ 3 = \dfrac{1 . 25 \times {10}^{3} \times v^{2}2}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) ⇒ v^{2}2 = \dfrac{6 \times 4}{1 . 25 \times {10}^{3} \times 3} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 8 \times {10}^{- 2}ms^{- 1}$

So, the discharge rate is,

${A}_{2}{v}_{2} = x \times {10}^{- 5} ⇒ x = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 8 \times {10}^{- 2}}{10- 5} = 4$

questions.q:
The area of cross-section of a large tank is $0 . 5m^{2}$. It has a narrow opening near the bottom having area of cross-section $1{cm}^{2}$. A load of $25$ kg is applied on the water at the top in the tank. Neglecting the speed of water in the tank, the velocity of the water, coming out of the opening at the time when the height of water level in the tank is $40$ cm above the bottom, will be _____~$cms^{- 1}$.

[Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pressure at point& $1$~is~${P}_{1} = {P}_{0}$, Pressure at point~$2$~is~${P}_{2} = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{mg}{A}$

Applying~Bernoulli's equation at top and bottom

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v1}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v2}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2} ⇒ {P}_{0} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρv^{2} + 0 = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{mg}{A} + 0 + ρgh$

$⇒ \dfrac{250}{5} + {10}^{3} \times 10 \times 0 . 4 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \times v^{2}$

$v = 3ms^{- 1} = 300cms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A liquid column of height $0.04 \mathrm{~cm}$ balances excess pressure of a soap bubble of certain radius. If density of liquid is $8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ and surface tension of soap solution is $0.28 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$, then diameter of the soap bubble is _____ $\mathrm{cm}$. (if $g=10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \rho \mathrm{gh}=\frac{4 \mathrm{~S}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\frac{4 \times 0.28}{8 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 4 \times 10^{-4}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{0.28}{8} \mathrm{~m}=\frac{28}{8} \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=3.5 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
Diameter $=7 \mathrm{~cm}$
